metadata.description: Expert-annotated gold standard triples from peer-reviewed scientific abstracts for extractor recall quantification

papers.title: A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions
papers.text: Understanding why a model makes a certain prediction is crucial. SHAP assigns each feature an importance value for a particular prediction. While SHAP addresses local explanation fidelity, it suffers from high computational overhead on deep neural networks.

papers.title: Why Should I Trust You?: Explaining the Predictions of Any Classifier
papers.text: LIME explains the predictions of any classifier by learning an interpretable model locally around the prediction. LIME evaluates on text classification benchmarks and improves user trust in machine learning models, but lacks theoretical convergence guarantees.

papers.title: Grad-CAM: Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-based Localization
papers.text: Grad-CAM uses gradient localization to produce visual explanations for convolutional networks. It addresses spatial saliency and compares with guided backpropagation baselines, though it lacks pixel-level fine-grained resolution.

papers.title: Axiomatic Attribution for Deep Networks
papers.text: Integrated Gradients improves attribution accuracy by satisfying completeness and implementation invariance. It addresses baseline selection sensitivity and uses path integrals, yet lacks computational speed during integration.

papers.title: Counterfactual Explanations without Opening the Black Box
papers.text: Counterfactual explanations improve algorithmic recourse by describing minimal input perturbations. They evaluate on tabular financial datasets and address user actionable feedback, but lack robustness under model retraining.

papers.title: Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps
papers.text: We show that widely used saliency maps contradict randomized weight baselines. The study evaluates on deep vision architectures and compares gradient saliency against edge detectors.

papers.title: Concept Activation Vectors for Interpretability
papers.text: TCAV uses directional derivatives to quantify concept importance. It improves domain expert interpretability, addresses semantic alignment, and applies to medical diagnostic images.

papers.title: TreeSHAP: Fast Explanations for Tree Ensembles
papers.text: TreeSHAP uses tree structure recursion to compute exact Shapley values in polynomial time. It addresses combinatorial explosion in decision trees and applies to XGBoost models.

papers.title: Fairness and Interpretability in Machine Learning
papers.text: We study fairness in attribution methods. The framework uses constrained optimization, addresses systemic bias in predictions, and lacks empirical validation across large-scale datasets.

papers.title: Adversarial Attacks on Explanation Methods
papers.text: Explanation manipulation methods deceive attribution frameworks without altering model predictions. We evaluate on ImageNet and demonstrate that gradient-based explainers use vulnerable sensitivity points.
